key_insight: Reasoning-structure graphs extracted from text provide a more robust signal for LLM authorship attribution than surface linguistic features.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical path for building detection systems that remain effective under paraphrasing, backtranslation, and model-version shifts.
method: Run an argument-mining pipeline to extract reasoning graphs from generated text.
Feed the graphs into a graph neural network for authorship attribution.
Compare against a Longformer baseline to test robustness and generalization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports gains of up to 27 percentage points under obfuscation attacks and 19 points on texts from unseen model versions.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable argument-mining graph extraction, which may be sensitive to parser errors and domain variation.
paper_title: Show Me How You Reason and I'll Tell You Who You Are: Reasoning Graphs for Robust LLM Authorship Attribution
